abstract: arXiv:2610.28673v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study the 305M-parameter audio encoder shared by Gemma 4 and EmbeddingGemma 2 (identical except for its final projection) for Saudi and Gulf Arabic speech recognition, without changing any of its weights. abstract: arXiv:2610.28686v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Query clarification is essential for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems that face ambiguous user queries. We consider multi-turn grounded conversational scenarios where a user query is either ill-formed or ambiguous in the context of the prior dialog or, more interestingly, it may be well-formed but when posed against retrieved documents there are multiple relevant interpretations. abstract: arXiv:2610.28693v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) enables low-cost and non-invasive heart rate (HR) monitoring but remains sensitive to waveform distortion, physiological variability, and measurement interference. Whether these gains extend to virtual worlds with different visual styles, dynamics, controls, and objectives remains unclear. abstract: arXiv:2610.28706v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-driven evolutionary search is a promising paradigm for scientific discovery, but existing methods remain costly and slow, often applying expensive reasoning uniformly while underusing evidence from failed, redundant, and saturated trials. abstract: arXiv:2610.28709v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Evaluating the energy transmission ratio of an X-ray beam through a polymer composite is a challenging task in radiation shielding studies. These include issues of copyright, ownership and bias, which apply to all types of data, whereas there are further issues particular to minoritised language communities and those on either side of the digital divide, as data is implicated in power imbalances and dynamics. title: Big Claims, Small Margins: Do Reported GraphLLM Gains Survive Simple Baselines?
abstract: arXiv:2610.28714v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM-based methods for node classification on text-attributed graphs (TAGs) routinely report state-of-the-art accuracy. We ask how these results compare with inexpensive baselines run on the same splits. title: Offline Apprenticeship Learning for Human-Centric Environments
abstract: arXiv:2610.28716v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Effective decision-making in human-centric environments such as Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITSs) and clinical healthcare requires policies that are adaptive, data-efficient, and ethically deployable. title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
abstract: arXiv:2610.28763v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Frontier coding agents are increasingly framed as end-to-end automated researchers, and ML for science offers a demanding test of that promise: improving a scientific model often requires domain insight beyond routine ML engineering. abstract: arXiv:2610.28766v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The development of face recognition has been strongly supported by the availability of large-scale training datasets. Among them, MS-Celeb-1M has played an important role by providing millions of facial images from nearly 100K identities. title: SkillEval: Learning Interpretable Ability Profiles of LLMs via Cognitive Diagnosis Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.28767v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Current evaluation of LLMs on benchmarks typically aggregates performance over individual examples into a single scalar score. This approach is overly coarse and ignores the diverse scope of skills covered by benchmark datasets. title: ReAPO: Retry-Aware Policy Optimization for Efficient Exploration in LLM Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2610.28770v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: RLVR improves language-model reasoning, but commonly relies on independent stochastic rollouts for exploration, which can repeatedly sample similar failed strategies. title: Motion Equivariant Convolutional LSTM: When Motion Becomes a Gauge Symmetry
abstract: arXiv:2610.28771v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Objects move, cameras pan, and weather drifts with the wind: much of what changes in sequential data is motion. Motion changes where things are, not what they are, and is therefore a symmetry of the data. Yet standard recurrent networks are not equivariant to it: their memory stays put while the input moves on. title: Scaling Therapy Supervision: Assessing Psychotherapy Fidelity Using Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.28772v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Psychotherapy fidelity assessment measures how faithfully a therapist adheres to a treatment protocol, a critical determinant of positive patient outcomes. However, fidelity assessment is bottlenecked by manual expert review, rendering the process labor-intensive and unscalable. abstract: arXiv:2610.28773v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Non-uniform allocation can improve post-training pruning of large language models, yet quality can still degrade sharply at high sparsity. To control degradation as sparsity increases, we introduce LADDER (Layer-Wise Allocation via Damage-Driven Evaluation and Refinement), which allocates sparsity incrementally. title: Complexity-Aware Surgical Video Reasoning Segmentation with Digital Twin and Context Memory
abstract: arXiv:2610.28776v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Conventional surgical segmentation relies on closed-set categories or explicit text queries, which cannot resolve implicit queries that require reasoning about workflows, instrument functions, and temporal relationships. title: Second Thoughts: Exploring and Planning through Comparative Imagination in World Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.28779v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: World models let agents compare imagined outcomes before acting, but an agent must still decide which alternatives to explore and when a proposed plan should replace its learned policy. We introduce SDI (Sibling Disagreement in Imagination), which connects these decisions through a shared actor-based reference. abstract: arXiv:2610.28784v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Aggressive low-state weight quantization can substantially reduce neural-network representational flexibility, making predictive performance difficult to preserve when only a few discrete weight states are available. We investigate this regime for Transformer-based electricity-load forecasting using 3-, 5-, 7-, and 16-state weight quantization across feed-forward-only and attention-plus-feed-forward quantization. title: Measure First, Then Allocate: Calibrated Rollout Budgets for MCP Agents in Reinforcement Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.28785v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Training tool-using language models requires costly interaction, yet identical rewards within a rollout group provide no group-relative learning signal. We use reward disagreement to guide harness evaluation and the allocation of rollouts for policy training in Model Context Protocol (MCP) environments. title: Is Anyone Enforcing the Cartel? What Reinforcement Learning Teaches LLM Agents in Markets
abstract: arXiv:2610.28787v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Evaluations of large language model (LLM) agents report that pricing agents collude at others' expense. Yet collusion is defined by enforcement: a cartel, in which competitors share monopoly profits, holds only if a member who cheats is punished. We introduce an audit that tests enforcement by forcing a member to cheat in counterfactual copies of a market, and use it to study what reinforcement learning (RL) teaches agents in pricing and trading.

title: ArcFlow: Training Flow Policies for Multiple Solver Budgets
abstract: arXiv:2610.28788v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Flow-matching policies adjust inference cost through the number of solver steps, but reinforcement learning at a single fixed solver budget can hide degradation at cheaper deployment budgets and even erase useful one-step behavior present in a pretrained policy. title: CALLIOPE: Private Insights into AI Use, Without Embeddings
abstract: arXiv:2610.28797v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We introduce CALLIOPE, a top-down framework for discovering topic hierarchies in large corpora of unstructured data (e.g., LLM conversations), while supporting differential privacy (DP). Unlike traditional and even recent LLM-augmented approaches that ultimately rely on clustering vector embeddings, our framework leverages LLM capabilities directly for the entire pipeline. title: An Explicit Feedback Contract for Iterative ML-Agent Harnesses
abstract: arXiv:2610.28798v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Iterative ML agents develop models by editing code, running experiments, reading a validation score, and choosing what to try next. In current harnesses this loop is served by an exact validation score returned after every attempt, which leaves the validation split open to adaptive selection. title: Where Do Legal Factors Live in LLMs?
abstract: arXiv:2610.28799v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In case-based legal reasoning, legal professionals identify legally significant fact patterns in a new dispute and compare them with those of decided cases. title: JUICE: Unified Multimodal Modeling in Pretrained Representation Spaces
abstract: arXiv:2610.28801v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Most unified multimodal models treat images and text asymmetrically: a pretrained language model generates text, an attached diffusion head generates images, and outputs that contain both are produced in a fixed order, so the first output cannot adapt to the second. title: Towards Realistic Models of Change: A Causal Perspective on Decision-Making and Dynamical Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.28803v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While statistical learning has made remarkable progress in recent decades, driven by large datasets and data-driven protocols that have transformed scientific practice, it still faces a key limitation: it struggles to generalize beyond the data it has seen, often failing under distribution shift. abstract: arXiv:2610.28806v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In vision and scientific domains involving spatial data, a key question is whether node feature values vary independently across space or form coherent spatial structures. Classical spatial autocorrelation statistics such as Moran's $I$ and Geary's $C$ quantify this phenomenon but operate on a single scalar variable with fixed neighbourhood weights, limiting their use for high-dimensional graph-like data. title: A Mechanistic Study of Automated Failure Attribution in LLM-based Agentic Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.28811v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agentic systems have demonstrated strong capabilities on complex tasks by enabling multiple interacting large language model (LLM)-based agents to collaborate and execute subtasks in parallel. title: Forging More Tasks into Better Harnesses: Agentic Harness Evolution via Successive Scale Racing
abstract: arXiv:2610.28815v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agentic harness evolution optimizes an agent's instructions, tools, and control flow by using its task execution experiences as evolving evidence. While more evolution tasks should intuitively improve performance, our preliminary study reveals a paradoxical failure mode: the performance of existing methods degrades as the task pool expands. abstract: arXiv:2610.28819v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Common instruction following (IF) benchmarks, such as IFEval, evaluate the ability of language models (LMs) to follow simple constraints that can easily be verified programmatically. title: Register Anything Model for Generalizable and Robust Point Cloud Registration
abstract: arXiv:2610.28821v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We present Register Anything Model (RAM), a unified model for generalizable 3D point cloud registration that robustly estimates 6-DoF transformations across diverse domains spanning sensors and environments. title: A Parallel Multi-Dialect Arabic Dependency Treebank
abstract: arXiv:2610.28823v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Dependency parsing resource development for Arabic has largely focused on Modern Standard Arabic, leaving dialectal Arabic comparatively under-resourced. We introduce MADARTB, the first large-scale parallel dependency treebank spanning five city dialects: Beirut, Cairo, Doha, Rabat and Tunis, and extending an existing parallel MSA version. title: Decision language models as affordable and rapid alternatives to LLM judges of clinical generative AI
abstract: arXiv:2610.28826v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Automated judges of clinical artificial intelligence (AI) outputs are necessary, but large language model (LLM) judges are costly and slow at scale. We compared Jev, a decision language model that returns structured judgments, with frontier and open-weight LLM judges in four use cases. abstract: arXiv:2610.28827v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We present WorldStream, an open-ended 3D world model with three simultaneous capabilities: it extends playable terrain beyond any pre-specified map, acts on open-ended language in the running world, and restores visited places with their edits. abstract: arXiv:2610.28829v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Instruction-guided video generative models offer a scalable solution for stress-testing autonomous driving systems by simulating diverse environmental conditions. title: Conditional Imaging for Privacy-Preserving Visual Sensing
abstract: arXiv:2610.28835v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Conventional visual sensing faces a fundamental dilemma: information that should remain private today may need to be recovered tomorrow. This challenge is becoming increasingly important as cameras become pervasive in our daily surroundings. Existing safeguards either protect visual content only after an image is formed or suppress information during capture in ways that prevent its later recovery. title: Sketch2Sim: an end-to-end modular framework for hand-drawn circuit analysis
abstract: arXiv:2610.28836v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This study proposes a sketch-to-simulation system to solve handwritten circuit diagrams. The system converts raw images into a Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis (SPICE)-compatible netlist and automatically calculates the circuit's nodal voltages and currents. title: How to Use Parallel Data for Multilingual Pretraining
abstract: arXiv:2610.28838v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: High-quality human-translated parallel corpora can improve cross-lingual transfer, but are typically too small for large-scale pretraining. Machine-translated web corpora help overcome this limitation, making parallel data available at pretraining scale. title: KIRA: A Full-Stack Reading Screening System with Dual-Pathway Analysis for Children
abstract: arXiv:2610.28840v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Early-grade reading screening is critical for identifying children at risk of reading difficulty. Existing AI-based screeners are often limited in the scope of their analyses and evaluation metrics, or are proprietary systems that lack transparent model specifications and evaluation. abstract: arXiv:2610.28843v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Visual question answering requires models to assign attributes and relations to the correct objects, a problem known as visual binding. Structured prompts make these assignments explicit through labeled fields. Yet an improvement from the full prompt does not reveal which labels help or how they interact. abstract: arXiv:2610.28849v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Latent diffusion models almost universally place a Gaussian prior on the VAE latent space. abstract: arXiv:2610.28855v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Progress on foundation model pretraining is gated by who can afford a trial, and relational pretraining is no exception. Recipes are developed inside individual labs, reported under private protocols, and do not accumulate. title: Depth-guided Geometric Adaptation for Few-shot Image Classification
abstract: arXiv:2610.28856v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Few-shot image classification (FSIC) frequently suffers from visual ambiguity, where background clutter and RGB appearance similarities hinder discriminative feature matching in data-scarce settings. To mitigate this, we propose DAFIC, a geometry-guided framework that incorporates monocular depth into representation learning, episodic adaptation, and dense support-query matching. title: DualHeads: Reward-tilted few-step diffusion made simple
abstract: arXiv:2610.28858v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Distilled diffusion models generate high-quality images in a few sampling steps, but aligning them with task requirements and human preferences is difficult. Methods developed for multi-step diffusion models rely on differentiable rewards, or on score fields and stochastic trajectories that distilled generators may lack. abstract: arXiv:2610.28864v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A systematic understanding of the global structure of neural-network loss landscapes remains challenging due to their high dimensionality. Symmetries arising from network architectures and learning objectives provide a way to investigate aspects of this structure. title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk, yet producing plausible continuations does not guarantee that they capture how scenes evolve. Under teacher forcing, strong temporal redundancy may allow local visual continuity to serve as a shortcut for current-chunk denoising, reducing the pressure to model visual evolution. title: DONIC: Generalist Dexterous Bimanual Tracking Control from Human Demonstrations
abstract: Despite recent progress in dexterous reference tracking, existing models focus primarily on single-hand manipulation and a limited range of interactions, leaving the bimanual dexterous behaviors common in real life unaddressed. title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
abstract: Autonomous agents powered by foundation models can reason, plan, and use tools, but their fixed weights and context limits hinder sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment. While external memory systems attempt to bridge this gap, they mostly act as passive retrieval caches, evaluated primarily by whether they can recall stored facts or past interactions. abstract: Using an LLM to generate training data for another is among the most general ways to train one, and it remains common practice. Some frontier teams have closed that route for their own models: what comes back is an answer, or a short summary, without the detailed reasoning trace behind it. title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
abstract: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback. title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Full 3D attention is costly in video Diffusion Transformers. Block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing only selected attention blocks. However, existing methods either overlook the potential to optimize sparsity allocation or rely on heuristic rules or local metrics to guide it. title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
abstract: World models turn visual representations into predictions and actions. We argue that their visual foundation should combine physical-state information, native language alignment, and pixel reconstruction, so that a single representation can support prediction, instruction, and inspection. However, existing encoders typically specialize in only one or two of these capabilities; we therefore introduce ALPS, a pretrained visual state encoder that unifies all three in a single set of patch tokens. title: RealMe: Immersive Volumetric Video from Minimal Captures
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of creating immersive volumetric videos from sparse and low-resolution capture resources. Conventional dense multi-view reconstruction methods can produce high-quality volumetric videos, but their reliance on costly capture setups makes them impractical in real-world scenarios. title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Agent harnesses have become a central component of modern agentic systems, shaping how models use tools, manage context, and coordinate long-horizon interaction. Realizing the benefits of these harnesses depends on how effectively the underlying model can make use of them, motivating reinforcement learning directly through the harness. However, existing approaches typically train through a single fixed harness, which can lead to specialization and limited transfer across harness configurations.

title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
abstract: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. title: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience
abstract: Spatial reasoning requires more than access to geometric tools: a reasoner must decide when direct observation is sufficient and when to reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames. We present SpatialBrain, a framework that retains experience about these decisions while keeping its vision-language backbone fixed. title: Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting
abstract: Most contemporary artificial intelligence (AI) systems are released with frozen parameters and improve through external updates, whereas an ideal system would keep improving from its own experience, a capacity we call recursive self-improvement (RSI). title: Agentic World Action Models
abstract: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
abstract: Linear-attention language models keep their context in a recurrent state of fixed size, where an inference system stores one copy of this state for every sequence it decodes at the same time.
